description: Canonical edge test-rig inventory. Read by scripts/fleet_health.py and documented in docs/edge-test-rigs.md. This file is the single source of truth for which rigs exist, how to reach them, what hardware they are expected to expose, and which Compose overlays they need.

rigs.name: dev dev/CI host + hardware rig

expectedHardware.description: Native Akida runtime service that owns port 8002
Prophesee EVK event camera on USB3 (disconnected as of 2026-09-17, CEL-299)

rigs.notes: Always-on box. Port 8002 belongs to the native neurochip.service; never evict it (see AGENTS.md). The containerized neurochip-hw-worker must stay stopped here, which is what docker-compose.akida-native.yml enforces.

rigs.name: hp-prodesk secondary test rig
rigs.notes: Reachability-only entry. The SSH user, expected services, and attached hardware are not yet recorded; add them here once confirmed. Empty expectedServices means the report lists every running container and flags any unhealthy one, rather than asserting a fixed set.

rigs.name: Windows + WSL2 self-hosted CI runner
rigs.notes: Sleeps when idle and wakes on demand via scripts/ci/runner-wake.sh; see docs/ci-runners.md. Runner status is read from the GitHub Actions runners API by label, so no SSH target is needed.

rigs.name: macOS self-hosted CI runner
rigs.notes: Host/IP not recorded. Set RELEASE_RUNNER_MACOS to the nmtk-mac label and register the runner per docs/ci-runners.md. Status is read from the GitHub Actions runners API by label.
